changelog:
[B][COLOR ff00fa9a]Version 1.0.89[/COLOR][/B]
[COLOR fffdb515]Audio languages in the source list[/COLOR]
-Each source now starts its line with the audio languages it carries: CAST, LAT, EN, FR and so on. Spanish from Spain and Latin American Spanish are told apart whenever the release says which one; when it only says Spanish, it shows ES rather than guessing.
-The languages come from the release name and from what the scrapers already send: the flags from Torrentio, Comet, MediaFusion and Peerflix, and the audio languages Easynews reports. Those were being received and thrown away. When the same torrent arrives from several scrapers, what any of them says counts for all of them.
-A language marked as subtitles, such as ITA.SUB, is not shown as audio.
-Choose a preferred audio language in Settings > Source Options > Audio languages. It is listed first on every source and highlighted, so a Spanish or French version stands out without reading the whole line.
[COLOR fffdb515]The real audio tracks, read before playback[/COLOR]
-Before a source plays, the add-on reads the track list inside the file itself: language, codec, channels, and which track is a commentary or an audio description. This is what the file really contains, not what its name claims.
-It reads the start of the file that the playback pre-flight has already downloaded, so it costs no extra request. With the pre-flight switched off, it downloads 1 MB. Files whose track list sits further in need one short extra request.
-Works with MKV and MP4.
-The tracks appear when playback starts. If your preferred language is not in the file, you are told at once. A Spanish track that does not say which Spanish is not reported as missing Castilian, because it may well be.
-A source that has already been read shows its real tracks in bold in the list the next time it appears, in place of what its name declared.
-Reading the tracks never blocks or skips a source, and anything it cannot read is simply left out.
